column1: # Old/new spelling pairs from the 1990 French orthographic reform
# ("Rectifications orthographiques du français"), sourced from the French
# Wiktionnaire annex page "Annexe:Rectifications orthographiques du français
# CC BY-SA) and cross-checked against the reform's own rule text (exceptions
# such as sûr/sûre keeping the circumflex are documented in that same page).
# Coverage: category 5 (accent grave replacing aigu, e.g. événement -> évènement),
# category 6 (circumflex removed from i/u, e.g. boîte -> boite), category 7 (tréma
# repositioned/added, e.g. aiguë -> aigüe), category 9 (-illier/-illière loses its "i",
# e.g. quincaillier -> quincailler), category 10 (-olle/-otter consonant doubling
# reduced, e.g. cocotter -> cocoter), category 12 (autres rectifications, a grab-bag of
# idiosyncratic per-word fixes, e.g. nénuphar -> nénufar) are populated here as sourced
# old/new pairs. Category 8 (-eler/-eter verb conjugation, e.g. amoncelle -> amoncèle)
# is NOT a static pair table -- it's implemented programmatically in lexique.py
# (loadElerEterQualifyingVerbs()) since it covers ~124 verbs generatively from Verbiste
# conjugation data rather than needing each conjugated form listed individually; see
# scratch/reform1990/STATUS.md for that mechanism's sourcing and validation, including a
# known gap (interpeller/interpeler, documented as an exception row below).
# Categories 2/4 (pluriels de mots composés, mots soudés) are NOT represented: ALL of
# their target words are hyphenated compounds, and hyphenated words never survive
# lexique.py's syllable-breakdown filter into LexiqueMixte.tsv at all (confirmed: 0
# hyphenated rows in the committed output), so there is nothing for an ortho-rewrite
# mechanism to touch even if built. Two categories (numéraux composés, participe passé de
# "laisser") are phrase/syntax-level rules with no row-level hook in a word lexicon at
# all -- see the two placeholder rows at the end, kept for completeness only.
# Category 3 (mots empruntés/loanwords) splits into two independent sub-categories,
# since a loanword can need either, both, or neither:
#   - "mots_empruntes_accent" -- the reform adds a French accent to a bare loanword
#     letter (e.g. arboretum -> arborétum). Mechanically identical to the other
#     accent-diacritic categories above: a single-character substitution/insertion,
#     appliesToOrthoRewrite=true, generalizes across the word's whole family exactly
#     like circonflexe/accent_grave/trema. Old spellings were found by trying every
#     accent-stripping of the sourced new spelling and checking corpus attestation
#   - "mots_empruntes_pluriel" -- the reform regularizes an irregular/foreign plural to
#     a plain French "-s" (e.g. un match, des matches -> des matchs). This is NOT a
#     single-character edit (barmen -> barmans, curricula -> curriculums are whole-suffix
#     replacements) and does NOT touch the singular row at all -- appliesToPluralRewrite
#     is a separate boolean/mechanism (lexique.py's loadReform1990PluralRewrites()) that
#     does a literal ortho match-and-replace restricted to number=="p" rows. Pairs were
#     only accepted where Lexique383 already has BOTH the reform's stated new plural
#     (from the Wiktionnaire subpage) AND some other, differing plural spelling under the
#     same lemme+number="p" (that differing spelling is the corpus's actual irregular
#     plural, not guessed) -- same "both independently attested" discipline as the rest
#     of this file, plus a gramCat/gender check per pair (see bêtasses/nues below for the
#     two danger cases that check caught).
# appliesToOrthoRewrite's transform is a single-character edit (substitution, deletion,
# OR insertion -- see lexique.py's computeSingleEditRule()) applied to a word's whole
# family (every corpus row sharing its lemme, or its exact ortho as a fallback for
# irregular forms like participles). Pairs needing a multi-character edit (e.g.
# nénuphar/nénufar's "ph"->"f", not a single insertion/deletion) are recorded here for
# completeness but NOT automated -- appliesToOrthoRewrite=False with a note explaining
# why, same treatment as an unattested pair.
# Candidate pairs were only accepted here when BOTH the old and new spelling
# are independently attested as real words in resources/Lexique383.tsv (see
# -- a reform spelling that never appears in the corpus can't cause a lemma
# clash in lexique.py either way, so it's out of scope for
# appliesToLemmeNormalization=true rows are the ones lexique.py's optional
# appliesToOrthoRewrite=true rows are the ones lexique.py's optional
# APPLY_1990_REFORM_ORTHO pass rewrites in place -- every corpus row whose
# ortho/lemme belongs to that word's family gets its ortho (and orthosyll_cv)
# updated to the new spelling, not just rows that already collide with an
# existing new-spelling row. This is what makes LexiqueMixte.tsv generative
# under the new norm instead of merely collision-free.
# appliesToPluralRewrite=true rows are the ones lexique.py's optional
# APPLY_1990_REFORM_EMPRUNT_PLURIEL pass rewrites -- a literal ortho match-and-replace
# on number=="p" rows only (oldSpelling here IS the full irregular plural form, not a
# lemme or a singular). Independent of the other three flags.
# isException=true rows must NOT be merged or rewritten -- either a
# documented reform exception (sûr/sûre keeps its circumflex) or a homograph
# collision with an unrelated, more common word (mûre/mure, fût/fut,
# faîte/faite) found during manual review, since automatic gramCat-overlap
# filtering proved unreliable (it both missed real collisions and flagged
# genuine pairs as false positives -- see scratch/reform1990/STATUS.md for
